CASE PUD 2026-000031 ENTRY NO. 141 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 08/31/2026 - PAGE 1 OF 4


           BEFORE THE CORPORATION COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF OKLAHOMA

     IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF                 )
     OKLAHOMA GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY                   )     CASE NO. PUD2026-000031
     FOR COMMISSION APPROVAL OF ELECTRIC                 )
     SERVICE AGREEMENTS AND PREAPPROVAL                  )
     OF CAPACITY PURCHASE AGREEMENTS                     )
     PURSUANT TO 17 O.S. § 286(C)                        )




                              SUMMARY OF RESPONSIVE TESTIMONY

                                                    OF

                                             JOHN GIVENS

                                            AUGUST 31, 2026
 CASE PUD 2026-000031 ENTRY NO. 141 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 08/31/2026 - PAGE 2 OF 4




    1          John Givens is employed by the Public Utility Division (“PUD”) of the Oklahoma

    2          Corporation Commission (“Commission”) as a Programs Manager V – Regulatory

    3          Depreciation Manager. On May 1, 2026, Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company (“OG&E”

    4          or “Company”) filed an Application with the Commission for approval of Electric Service

    5          Agreements (“ESA”) between the Company and Google subsidiary Alliance Site and Grid,

    6          LLC (“Google”), and preapproval of Capacity Purchase Agreements (“CPA”) pursuant to

    7          17 O.S. § 286(C). Mr. Givens filed Responsive Testimony on August 5, 2026, to present

    8          PUD’s analysis and recommendations regarding the ESAs and CPAs proposed by OG&E,

    9          and to recommend a method for reviewing customer impacts.



   10          Mr. Givens testified that PUD reviewed the relevant rules and statutes that govern

   11          Commission preapproval of new generation capacity. In addition, Mr. Givens testified that

   12          PUD reviewed the Direct Testimony and associated workpapers filed by Company

   13          witnesses, issued data requests and reviewed the responses, and reviewed responses to data

   14          requests issued by other parties to this Case, including confidential and highly

   15          sensitive confidential information provided for review through a secure web portal. Mr.

   16          Givens further testified that PUD reviewed Commission orders, testimony, and workpapers

   17          from prior OG&E cases and held a virtual audit conference to discuss the Case with

   18          Company personnel.



   19          Mr. Givens testified that as a result of its review, PUD makes the following

   20          recommendations:

   21              •   ESAs: PUD recommends that the Commission find that the Supplemental Resource
   22                  Administrative Charge is reasonable, and that the ESAs contain reasonable

    1                  customer protections that meet the requirements of Oklahoma House Bill 2992
    2                  (2026). PUD also recommends that the Commission find it is likely that existing
    3                  customers will receive some benefit from the ESAs, but that the Company’s $130
    4                  million savings estimate could overstate that benefit given the uncertainty
    5                  surrounding how marginal ESA costs will be functionalized, classified, and
    6                  assigned within a future cost of service study.

    7              •   CPAs: PUD recommends that the Commission find there is a need for the CPA
    8                  resources. However, PUD also recommends that the Commission carefully
    9                  scrutinize the Company’s decision to compare the CPAs against bids received in a
   10                  prior Request for Proposal (“RFP”) and only grant preapproval if it finds that
   11                  evaluation of reasonable alternatives was impossible because the pricing under the
   12                  CPAs is so favorable that any possible alternatives would be facially unreasonable.
   13                  This sets an intentionally high bar to discourage utilities from evading RFP
   14                  requirements and instead comparing resources to old, possibly outdated bids. PUD
   15                  further recommends that the Commission make clear that, in future cases,
   16                  comparing a non-bid resource to the results of a closed, prior RFP does not
   17                  necessarily satisfy the obligation to consider reasonable alternatives.

   18              •   Customer Impact Review: PUD recommends that the Company annually assess
   19                  adverse rate impacts from the Google ESAs on other customer classes, and that any
   20                  such impacts be booked to an offsetting regulatory asset and regulatory liability.
   21                  These accounts would be subject to review in a future rate case, and could be
   22                  assigned back to the other classes. This will ensure that adverse impacts, if any,
   23                  would not only cease going forward when new rates become effective, but impacts
   24                  experienced between rate cases could also be mitigated.




                                     Summary of Responsive Testimony – Givens
                            Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company – Case No. PUD2026-000031
